subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Elastic Potential Energy in Everyday Life
description: Learn Elastic Potential Energy in Everyday Life in one minute.

hook.text: Pull back a rubber band. You can feel the stored energy. Release it and that energy launches across the room.

buildup.text: Elastic potential energy is stored in any deformed material — bent bows, compressed foam, stretched tendons.

discovery.text: The energy equals half times k times x squared. Small compressions store little. Big ones store a lot.

twist.text: Pole vaulters store energy in a bending pole, then convert it into height. The pole is a spring.

climax.text: Running shoes use foam that stores and returns energy with each stride. Your shoe is a spring too.

punchline.text: Bend it, stretch it, squeeze it — energy waits inside.

quiz.question: What does a pole vaulter's bending pole demonstrate?
options: Kinetic energy converting directly into gravitational potential energy
Elastic potential energy stored in the bent pole converting into height
Friction reducing the vaulter's speed as they leave the ground
